verdict: Synthetic augmentation reliably improves macro-F1: +0.055 (95% CI +0.027 to +0.080).
uses: Augment the real training set with ddpm_unet samples at the planned ratio when training the downstream classifier.

A classifier trained on synthetic data alone reaches 90% of the real-data macro-F1: the samples carry most of the class signal and are suitable for pipeline prototyping, teaching and method development where real data cannot be shared.
No memorization signal (DCR ratio 1.06, 0.7% too close vs ~5% expected); privacy still requires a formal guarantee (e.g. differential privacy) before external release.
warnings: Never use synthetic samples as test or validation data: performance must be measured on held-out real data.
Do not estimate population quantities (prevalence, class proportions, effect sizes, differential-expression statistics) from synthetic samples; they reflect the generator, not new evidence.
Label synthetic records as synthetic wherever they are stored or shared; never pool them with real data in a way that hides their origin.
